latest.description: Learn to build your first quantum circuit on AWS. Master the Hadamard gate, explore superposition, and get started with Amazon Braket.

latest.title: AWS Amplify Evolution Timeline — 2017 to 2025
latest.description: AWS Amplify has evolved over 8 years from a complex setup in 2017 to a weekend-friendly, code-first platform in 2025. Key updates like the CLI, Console, Next.js support, Gen 2 (TypeScript-first), and the AI Kit have removed manual chores like IAM and infrastructure management. Developers can now build production-grade, offline-ready, and secure SaaS prototypes in a single weekend.

latest.title: Building a Static Website for the King of Pop on AWS
latest.description: Go beyond a basic "Hello World" website and build a tribute to the King of Pop while mastering AWS fundamentals. In this hands-on tutorial, you'll create and deploy a responsive static website using Amazon S3, enable website hosting, and make your project accessible to the world. Whether you're learning AWS or looking for a fun project to showcase your cloud skills, this guide combines technical practice with a tribute to one of music's greatest icons.

latest.title: A Roadmap to AWS Amplify Gen2: Shifting Your Mindset from Gen1 to a Modern, AWS-Integrated Frontend CI/CD Platform
latest.description: AWS Amplify has evolved from Gen1’s simple hosting into Gen2, a powerful, flexible CI/CD platform integrated with core AWS resources like CloudFront and S3. Gen2 introduces key upgrades: optimized builds with intelligent caching, improved env var and IAM permission management, and custom CDN tuning. Additionally, long-awaited native WAF support was added on Dec 18, 2024. Migrating to Gen2 is a great chance to modernize your workflows and build a faster, more secure frontend development environment.

latest.title: Aiming for sustainable community management - Improvement of Amplify Japan User Group's management system in 2023
latest.description: AWS Community Builder @ikenyal shares how they improved the management of the Amplify Japan User Group in 2023. As a volunteer group, they faced stagnation due to shifting to community-led operations. To ensure sustainability, they implemented key changes: clarifying active members with annual check-ins, setting up monthly meetings, and migrating to free tools like GitHub Discussions for docs and Discord for logs. They also boosted team unity with custom T-shirts to maintain motivation.

latest.title: AI Engineer Happy Hour
latest.description:
A low-key happy hour for AI engineers, technical founders, and product builders who are actively building with agents, coding tools, retrieval, evals, model APIs, infrastructure, and AI-native workflows.
Just a useful room of people comparing notes on what is working, what is breaking, and what they are building next.

latest.title: From PHP Shared Hosting to the Serverless Edge: Rebuilding Last2Lines with Vercel v0 and AWS Aurora
latest.description: Last2Lines is an AI-powered social campaigning platform that unites global voices by having the world write a single poem, two lines at a time. To scale my advocacy efforts, I joined the "Hackathon: H0: Hack the Zero Stack with Vercel v0 and AWS Databases" hackathon where I  completely re-architected the platform into a production-ready powerhouse using Vercel and AWS.

latest.title: From 24GB to 7.8GB: Quantizing Gemma 4 12B with GPTQ and Serving on a Single L4 GPU
latest.description: A first-principles, end-to-end account of compressing Google's Gemma 4 12B multimodal model from 24GB to 7.8GB with GPTQ W4A16 and serving it on a single NVIDIA L4 GPU using vLLM. Covers the GPTQ algorithm, the multimodal ignore-list minefield, a subtle config.json metadata bug, version conflicts, and the FlashInfer JIT compilation saga — with every real error message, diagnosis, and fix included.

latest.title: Building AI Agents with Amazon Nova Pro and Strands SDK: My AWS Nova Sprint Journey
latest.description: This article documents my learning journey through the AWS Nova Sprint – April Edition organized by AWS User Group Madurai. It covers how I built AI-powered applications using Amazon Nova Pro on Amazon Bedrock, explored the Strands SDK, integrated tools and memory, and implemented Model Context Protocol (MCP) to create an AWS Documentation Assistant. The article shares practical code examples, key learnings, challenges encountered, and best practices for developers getting started with AI agents on AWS.

latest.title: How I Used Amazon Quick to Supercharge My CFP Submissions as an AWS Community Builder
latest.description: As an AWS Community Builder in the AI Engineering category, I'm always looking for ways to apply the services I advocate for to real problems I face. CFP season is one of those problems.

trending.description: System Design felt overwhelming when I started at Amazon. There were too many terms, too much to learn, no clear starting point. trending.title: AIdeas Finalist: ASET – Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth
trending.description:
ASET (Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth) is a scientific claim verification engine built  for the AI era — where information can be generated instantly, but trust cannot, to address the growing problem of hallucinated citations and  AI-generated information.

Instead of probabilistic prediction, ASET retrieves, analyzes, and synthesizes evidence from 1.2M+ indexed research papers to produce literature-backed verification reports for claims extracted from text, documents, webpages, images, and videos.
